newsitem.title: INDIA: India call rates end lower, gilt prices rally.
newsitem.headline: India call rates end lower, gilt prices rally.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed at 2.00-2.25 percent on Wednesday, lower from the day's opening levels of 3.00-4.00 percent, dealers said.
"The call rates are ruling below 4.0 percent and there is a possibility of arbitrage between tap bill and call money," a dealer a government bank said.
In the event of such an arbitrage, call rates would rally above 5.0 percent level, he said.
Yields on securities continued to fall on Wednesday and the market was very bullish on government securities, Joseph Thomas, a senior manager at Ceat Financial Servises said.
Thomas said the trend will continue till the liquidity position remained easy and the call rates subdued.

"Because of less interest from borrowers, money was diverted into the security market, pushing up demand for short-dated securities and treasury bills," Felix D'cunna, a dealer at Tower Capital and Securities, said.
The volume on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) was 4.25 billion rupees against the Tuesday's volume of 4.50 billion rupees, D'cunna said.

The yield on 13.50 percent 1997 stock fell on Wednesday to 11.26 percent against Tuesday's 11.78 percent, while yield on 13.50 percent 1998 converted stock, slipped to 12.11 percent from the Tuesday's 12.48 percent, a dealer said.
He said the yield on zero coupon bond maturing in 2000 fell to 13.47 percent from Tuesday's 13.57 percent.
Commercial papers were quoted at 12.00-13.00 percent for P1+ rated companies and certificate of deposits were at 11.50-12.50 percent, dealers said.
Inter-corporate deposits were quoted at 17-18.5 percent for 90 days for P1+ companies, while the P1 companies were quoted in the region of 21-27 percent.
